semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {يَغْشَى الناس}: a second adjective (ṣifa), meaning "with a clear smoke that envelops."
His saying: «هذا عَذابٌ» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; and that saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "saying that." It is also possible that it is not governed by any saying at all, but is a mere statement of information.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {أنى لَهُمُ الذكرى}: it is possible that «أنَّى» is the khabar (predicate) of «ذِكْرى», with «لهم» serving as a clarification. It is also possible that «أنَّى» is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), attached to the settled-in-place meaning in «لهم», since «لهم» has occurred as the khabar of «ذِكْرى».
His saying: «وقد جاءَهم» is a ḥāl from «لهم». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «مُعَلِّم» with kasra on the lām.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {قَلِيلاً}: an adjective of an omitted time or verbal noun, i.e. "a little removal" or "a little time."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ}: it is said that it is a badal (substitute) for «يَومَ تأتي». It is said that it is accusative through an implied "remember" (udhkur). It is said that it is governed by «مُنْتَقِمون». And it is said that it is governed by what «مُنْتَقِمون» points to, namely "he takes vengeance" (yantaqim). This last was rejected on the ground that what follows «إنَّ» does not operate on what precedes it, and that only what is able to operate may be the thing that is explained.
His saying: «نَبْطِش»: the majority read it with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the ṭāʾ, i.e. "we seize them." al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read it with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, which is a dialectal form of the imperfect of بَطَشَ. al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Ṭalḥa read it with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the ṭāʾ, which is transferred from بَطَشَ, i.e. "the angels seize them." On this reading «البَطْشَةَ» may be accusative through «نُبْطِشُ» with the extra element dropped, like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]; or it may be accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "the angels seize them, so they seize the seizure."

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا}: it was read «فَتَّنَّا» with shadda, for intensification or multiplication, because of the multiplicity of what it relates to. And «جاءهم رسولٌ» may be resumptive (istiʾnāf) or a ḥāl.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {أَنْ أدوا}: it may be the explicative (mufassira), because something with the sense of saying precedes it; it may be the lightened (mukhaffafa) one; and it may be the one that puts the imperfect in the subjunctive, which is connected to an imperative. There is a difficulty, mentioned earlier, in taking it as the lightened one: the khabar in this chapter does not occur as a request. And if it is taken as a maṣdar particle, it is with the preposition omitted, i.e. "he came to them with (the message) that you hand over." «عبادَ الله» may be a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). It is said in the exegesis that he asked them to hand over to him the Children of Israel, and {فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِيَ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} indicates this. Or it may be a vocative (munādā), with the object omitted, i.e. "give me obedience, O servants of Allah."

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {وَأَن لاَّ تَعْلُواْ}: conjoined (ʿaṭf) to the first «أَنْ». The majority read «إنِّي آتِيْكم» with kasra on the hamza, as resumptive. It was also read with fatḥa, assuming a lām, i.e. "and that you do not exalt yourselves, because I am bringing you…"

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {أَن تَرْجُمُونِ}: i.e. "from your stoning me" (min an tarjumūn).
And his saying: «إنِّي عُذْتُ» is resumptive. Abū ʿAmr and the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) assimilated the dhāl into the tāʾ. Its justification has already been given in Ṭāhā at his saying {فَنَبَذْتُهَا} [Ṭāhā: 96].

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {أَنَّ هؤلاء}: the majority read it with fatḥa, with an implied preposition, i.e. "he called upon him with (the plea) that these…". Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā and al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, with an implied saying according to the Basrans, and by treating «دَعا» like "said" according to the Kufans.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي}: the two readings with connecting and cutting hamza have been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī said: "There are two aspects to it: an implied saying after the fāʾ, i.e. 'so He said: travel by night with My servants'; or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, as if He had said: 'if the matter is as you say, then travel by night with My servants.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "He often claims the omission of the condition, but that is not permitted except with clear evidence, such as an imperative or the like preceding it."

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {رَهْواً}: it may be a second object, on the basis that «تَرَكَ» means "made" (ṣayyara); or a ḥāl, on the basis that it does not have that meaning. As for الرَّهْو, it is said to mean stillness, so the meaning is "leave it still." One says: رَهَا يَرْهُوا رَهْواً. From this comes "the horses came رَهْواً." al-Nābigha said:
4014 - والخيلَ تَمْزَعُ رَهْواً في أَعِنَّتِها ... كالطيرِ تَنْجُوْ مِنَ الشُّؤْبوب ذي البَرَدِ
(The horses run smoothly in their bridles, like birds escaping a downpour with hail.)
And رَهَا يَرْهُو in his walking means he went gently. al-Qaṭāmī said:
4015 - يَمْشِيْنَ رَهْواً فلا الأَعْجازُ خاذِلَةٌ ... ولا الصدورُ على الأعجازِ تَتَّكِلُ
(They walk gently; the hindquarters do not fail, nor do the chests rely on the hindquarters.)
From Abū ʿUbayda: رَهْواً means "leave it open, in gaps, as you left it."
In the exegesis: when the sea split for Moses and he came up out of it, he feared that Pharaoh would follow him, so he wished to strike it so that it would return and they would not catch up with him. He was commanded to leave it in gaps. Its origin is from their saying: / رَها الرجلُ يَرْهُو رَهْواً, when the man parted what is between his legs. الرَّهْو and الرَّهْوَة mean a place that is both elevated and low, where (water) collects, so it is one of the contronyms (aḍdād). الرَّهْوَة is also the woman with a wide private part. And الرَّهْو is a bird, said to be the crane. The discussion of the parallel to {كَمْ تَرَكُواْ مِن جَنَّاتٍ} has already been given in al-Shuʿarāʾ.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {وَمَقَامٍ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the mīm, which is a noun of place, the place of standing. Ibn Hurmuz, Qatāda, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ, and Nāfiʿ in the transmission of Khārija read it with ḍamma, a noun of place from أقام.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
And النَّعْمَة with fatḥa means the freshness and delight of life. The majority read it as genitive. Abū Rajāʾ made it accusative, conjoined to «كم», i.e. "they left much of such-and-such, and they left a pleasant life."
His saying: «فاكِهين»: the majority read it with alif, meaning "of good spirit" or "possessors of fruit" like لابن (possessor of milk) and تامر (possessor of dates). It is also said: فاكهين means "heedless, amusing themselves." al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read «فَكِهين», meaning "treating lightly, mocking." al-Jawharī said: "One says: فَكِهَ الرجلُ, with kasra, and he is فَكِهٌ when he is a joker; and الفَكِهُ also means the insolent (al-ashir)."

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: the kāf may be nominative in position, as khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus"; al-Zajjāj inclined to this. It may also be accusative in position; al-Ḥūfī implied: "We destroyed (them) a destruction, and took vengeance a vengeance, like that." al-Kalbī said: "Thus I do to whoever disobeys Me." It is also said that the implied form is "He does a deed like that." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "a leaving like that," making it an adjective of the omitted "leaving." On all these aspects one stops at «كذلك» and begins «وأَوْرَثْناها». al-Zamakhsharī said: "The kāf is accusative in the sense of: 'in the likeness of that expulsion We expelled them from it, and We made another people, not of them, inherit it.'" On this view «وأَوْرَثْناها» is conjoined to that clause which governs the kāf, and so stopping at «كذلك» is not permitted.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السمآء}: it may be a metaphor (istiʿāra), like the saying of al-Farazdaq:
4016 - الشمسُ طالِعَةٌ ليسَتْ بكاسِفَةٍ ... تَبْكي عليك نجومَ الليلِ والقمرا
(The sun is rising, not eclipsed; the stars of the night and the moon weep for you.)
Jarīr said:
4017 - لَمَّا أتى خبرُ الزُّبَيْرِ تواضَعَتْ ... سُوْرُ المدينةِ والجبالُ الخُشَّعُ
(When the news of al-Zubayr came, the walls of the city humbled themselves, and the submissive mountains.)
al-Nābigha said:
4018 - بكى حارِثُ الجَوْلانِ مِنْ فَقْدِ رَبِّهِ ... وحَوْرَانُ منه خاشِعٌ مُتَضائِلُ
(Ḥārith of al-Jawlān wept for the loss of his lord, and Ḥawrān, humbled by it, shrank.)

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {مِن فِرْعَوْنَ}: there are two aspects to it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) for «العذاب», either with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from the torment of Pharaoh," or by way of exaggeration, making him the very torment itself and so substituting him for it. The second: it is a ḥāl from «العذاب», its implied form being "proceeding from Pharaoh."
ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read {مِنَ عَذَابِ المهين}, which is the annexation of the qualified noun to its attribute, since the original is "the humiliating torment," as in the well-known reading.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «مَنْ فرعونُ» with fatḥa on the mīm of «مَنْ» and nominative «فرعونُ», as mubtadaʾ and khabar; it is a question of contempt, like your saying "Who are you and Zayd?" Then He explained his state by the clause that follows, in His saying {إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَالِياً مِّنَ المسرفين}.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {على عِلْمٍ عَلَى العالمين}: the first «على» is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the agent in «اخْتَرْناهم». The second is attached to «اخْتَرْناهم». In the Shaykh's (Abū Ḥayyān's) wording: since their meanings differ, it is permissible for both to be attached to «اخْتَرْنا». The Shaykh recited a parallel to that:
4019 - ويَوْماً على ظَهْر الكَثِيْبِ تَعَذَّرَتْ ... عليَّ وآلَتْ حَلْفَةً لم تَحَلَّلِ
(And one day, on the back of the sand dune, she was unyielding toward me and swore an oath she did not absolve.)
Then he said: "So «على عِلْم» is a ḥāl, either from the agent or from the object; and «على ظَهْر» is a ḥāl from the agent in «تَعَذَّرَتْ». The operator in the ḥāl is the operator in its owner." There is something to consider here: his first statement, "and therefore both are attached to one verb when the meanings differ," contradicts making the first a ḥāl, because then it is not attached to the verb. And his statement "the operator in the ḥāl is the operator in its owner" does not help in that.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {والذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ}: three aspects are possible. The first: it is conjoined to «قومُ تُبَّع». The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is what follows, namely «أَهْلَكْناهم». As for the first aspect, «أَهْلَكْناهم» is either resumptive or a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the ṣila. The third: it is accusative through an implied verb which «أَهْلَكْناهم» explains. In that case «أَهْلكنا» has no grammatical position.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {لاَعِبِينَ}: a ḥāl. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «وما بينَهُنَّ» because the heavens and the earth are a plural. The majority read «بينَهما», considering the two kinds.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ بالحق}: a ḥāl, either from the agent, which is the apparent view, or from the object, i.e. "except as ones acting rightly" or "ones joined/ with the truth."

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {إِنَّ يَوْمَ الفصل مِيقَاتُهُمْ}: the majority read «ميقاتُهم» as nominative, the khabar of «إنَّ». It was also read as accusative, as the ism (subject) of «إنَّ», with «يومَ الفصلِ» as its khabar. And «أَجْمعين» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the genitive pronoun.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ لاَ يُغْنِي}: it may be a badal from «يومَ الفصل», or an explicative apposition (bayān) according to those who do not require agreement in definiteness and indefiniteness; it may be accusative through an implied "I mean" (aʿnī); or it may be an adjective of «مِيقاتُهم», though it is indeclinable (buniya). Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. But this is not possible according to the Basrans, because it is annexed to an inflected word. This was discussed earlier, at the end of al-Māʾida. It may also be accusative through a verb that «يومَ الفَصْلِ» points to, i.e. "He decides between them on a day when… no benefit." It is not permitted for it to be accusative through «الفصل» itself, because that would entail a separation between the two by an outsider, namely «ميقاتُهم», and «الفَصْل» is a maṣdar, in which that is not permitted. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because it has already been predicated about," and there is looseness in this, since predicating about what is annexed to «الفَصْل» does not negate «الفَصْل».
His saying: «ولا هم»: the pronoun is plural, referring back to «مَوْلَى», although it is singular, because the meaning was intended and so it was pluralised; and it is indefinite in a context of negation, so it is general.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ الله}: four aspects are possible. The first, which is the saying of al-Kisāʾī: it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ). The second: it is connected, its implied form being "no relative avails another relative, except the believers, for they will be permitted to intercede, and they will intercede for some of one another." The third: it is nominative as a badal for the first «مَوْلَى», with «يُغْني» meaning "benefits"; al-Ḥūfī said this. The fourth: it is also nominative in position, as a badal for the wāw of «يُنْصَرُون», i.e. "none will be protected from the torment except whom Allah has shown mercy."

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {كالمهل}: it may be a second khabar, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is like molten brass (al-muhl)." It is not permitted to be a ḥāl from «طعام الأثيم». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because there is then no operator." There is something to consider here, because it is permissible for it to be a ḥāl, with the operator in it being the sense of comparison, as in your saying "Zayd is your brother, courageous."
الأَثيم is an intensive adjective. One also says الأَثُوم, like الصَّبور and الشَّكور. As for المُهْل: it is said to be the dregs of oil. It is said to be the sediment of tar. It is said to be what is melted of gold or silver. And it is said to be what is melted of them and of everything similar among the malleable metals, such as iron, copper and lead. المَهْل with fatḥa means calm and gentleness. From it comes {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين} [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. al-Ḥasan read «كالمَهْل» with fatḥa on the mīm only, which is a dialectal form of المُهْل with ḍamma.
His saying: «يَغْلي»: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read it with yāʾ (below). The agent is a pronoun referring back to the food (ṭaʿām). Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to refer to the zaqqūm. It is said it refers to the muhl itself, and «يَغْلي» is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition-phrase, i.e. "resembling the muhl, boiling." It may be a ḥāl from the muhl itself. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it boils," meaning the zaqqūm or the food. The rest read «تَغْلي» with tāʾ (above), the agent being a pronoun for the tree; the clause is then a second khabar, or a ḥāl according to one opinion, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it boils."

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {كَغَلْيِ الحميم}: an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl from its pronoun, i.e. "it boils a boiling like the boiling of scalding water," or "it boils it, resembling the boiling of scalding water."

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {فاعتلوه}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «اعْتُلوه» with ḍamma on the ʿayn. The others read it with kasra. They are two dialectal forms in the imperfect of عَتَله, meaning to drag him with harshness and coarseness, like عَرَش يَعْرِش and يَعْرُش. And العُتُلّ means the harsh, coarse one.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {إِنَّكَ أَنتَ}: al-Kisāʾī read it with fatḥa in the sense of cause, i.e. "because you." It is also said that the implied form is: "Taste the torment of (the fact) that you are the mighty one." The others read it with kasra, as resumptive conveying the cause, so the two readings converge in meaning. This speech is by way of mockery, which is more infuriating to the one mocked. Similar is the saying of Jarīr to a poet who called himself "the flower of Yemen":
4020 - ألَمْ يَكُنْ في وُسُومٍ قد وَسَمْتُ بها ... مَنْ كان موعظةً يا زهرةَ اليَمَنِ
(Was there not, in the brands I have branded with, a warning for whoever needed one, O flower of Yemen?)
That poet had said:
4021 - أبْلِغْ كُلَيْباً وأَبْلِغْ عَنْك شاعرَها ... أنِّي الأَغَرُّ وأنِّي زهرةُ اليمنِ
(Convey to Kulayb, and convey on your behalf to its poet, that I am the radiant one and I am the flower of Yemen.)

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {فِي جَنَّاتٍ}: / it may be a badal for His saying «في مَقام» with repetition of the operator, or it may be a second khabar.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {يَلْبَسُونَ}: it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the preposition-phrase, or the khabar of «إنَّ» with the preposition-phrase attached to it, or resumptive.
His saying: «مُتقابلين»: a ḥāl from the agent of «يَلْبَسون». The explanation of these words, السُّنْدس, الإِستبرق and المقام, has already been given.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: there are two aspects to this kāf. The first: accusative, as an adjective of a maṣdar, i.e. "We do to the God-fearing a deed like that," i.e. like that deed. The second: nominative, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus." Abū l-Baqāʾ implied before it a circumstantial clause, saying: "its implied form is: we did that, and the matter is thus"; there is no need for this. One stops at «كذلك» and begins with His saying «وزَوَّجْناهم».
His saying: «بِحُوْرٍ عِيْنٍ»: the majority read «حور» with tanwīn, described by «عِيْن». ʿIkrima did not give it tanwīn; he annexed them, because they divide into wide-eyed (ʿīn) and not wide-eyed. The explanation of الحُور العين has already been given.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {يَدْعُونَ}: a ḥāl from the object of «زَوَّجْناهم», and its object is omitted, i.e. "they call the servants for every fruit."
His saying: «آمِنين»: it may be a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the agent of «يَدْعُون», in which case it is a nested ḥāl.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {لاَ يَذُوقُونَ}: it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «آمِنين», or a third or second ḥāl from the object of «زَوَّجْناهم», with «آمنين» a ḥāl from the agent of «يَدْعُون» as stated earlier, or an adjective of «آمِنين», or resumptive. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «لا يُذاقون» in the passive.
His saying: {إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى}: there are several aspects. The first: it is a disconnected exception, i.e. "but they have already tasted the first death." The second: it is connected, and they interpreted it thus: the believer at his death in this world is in the position of being in Paradise, because of seeing what he will be given of it, or because of his certainty of its bliss. The third: «إلاَّ» is in the sense of "other than" (siwā); al-Ṭabarī reported this and judged it weak. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His judging it weak is not correct; rather its being in the sense of siwā is sound and coherent." The fourth: «إلاَّ» is in the sense of "after" (baʿd). al-Ṭabarī preferred it, and the majority rejected it, because «إلاَّ» in the sense of "after" is not established. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is the first death, which is tasted before entering Paradise, excepted from the death whose tasting is negated? I say: it was intended to say 'they will not taste death there at all,' so He put His saying {إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى} in the place of that; for tasting the past death in the future is impossible, so it is of the type of suspension upon the impossible: as if it were said, 'if the first death could be tasted in the future, then they will taste it in Paradise.'" I say: among the scholars of rhetoric this is called negating a thing by means of its proof. Similar is the saying of al-Nābigha:
4022 - لا عَيْبَ فيهم غيرَ أنَّ سيوفَهُمْ ... بهنَّ فُلولٌ مِنْ قِراعِ الكتائبِ
(There is no fault in them, except that their swords have nicks from striking the battalions.)
He means: if anyone counts the nicks of swords from striking battalions a fault, then this is their fault; but counting it among faults is impossible, so fault is negated from them by the proof of suspending the matter upon an impossibility. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, after what I earlier related from al-Ṭabarī: "So He made clear that He negated tasting death from them, and that nothing reaches them of it beyond what preceded in this world." He means that it is speech to be taken according to its meaning.
His saying: «ووَقاهم»: the majority read it lightened. Abū Ḥaywa read «ووقَّاهم» with shadda for intensification, and it is not for transitivity, since it already governs two objects before that.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {فَضْلاً}: this is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and that is what Makkī meant when he said: "a maṣdar that «يَدْعُون» operates on." It is said that the operator in it is «ووَقاهم»; it is said, «آمِنين»; but this only appears sound if it is an object of purpose. It is also possible that it is a maṣdar, because «يَدْعُون» and what follows are of the type of bestowing favour, so it is a maṣdar concurring with its operator in meaning. Abū l-Baqāʾ made it accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "We bestowed that as a favour," i.e. as bestowal.

semin-durr:58-58.t: His saying: {يَسَّرْنَاهُ}: i.e. the Qur'an, in your tongue, i.e. in your language. The bāʾ is for accompaniment./

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {فارتقب إِنَّهُمْ مُّرْتَقِبُونَ}: the two objects of "watching" (irtiqāb) are omitted, i.e. "so watch for victory from your Lord; they are watching, with regard to you, what they wish for of reversals and treacheries, but that will never harm you."

semin-durr:3-3.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: {إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَاهُ}: it may be the answer to the oath, or it may be parenthetical, the answer being His saying {إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ}, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya preferred it. It was also said: «إنَّا كُنَّا» is resumptive, or a second answer without a conjunction.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ}: it may be resumptive, or an adjective of «ليلة» with what is between them parenthetical. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: 'إنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرين' and 'فيها يُفْرَقُ', what is the position of these two sentences? I say: they are two resumptive sentences, folded together (malfūfatān), by which he explained the answer of the oath, which is «أَنْزَلْناه», as if it were said: 'We sent it down because it is in Our nature to warn and caution, and Our sending it down in this night in particular was because the sending down of the Qur'an is among the wise matters, and this night is the one in which every wise matter is distinguished.'" I say: this is among the fine points of this man.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash read «يَفْرُقُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the rā', and «كلَّ» accusative, i.e. "Allah distinguishes every matter". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نَفْرِقُ» with the nūn of majesty, «كلَّ» accusative, so al-Zamakhsharī reported; and al-Ahwāzī reported from him «يَفْرِق» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the rā', «كلَّ» accusative, «حكيمٌ» nominative as the agent of «يَفْرِق». From al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash also: «يُفَرَّقُ» like the majority, except with doubling.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {أَمْراً}: it has twelve analyses. The first: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «أَنْزَلْناه». The second: it is a ḥāl from its object, i.e. "We sent it down commanding", or "commanded". The third: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its accusative-assigner is either «أَنْزَلْناه», or «مُنْذرِين», or «يُفْرَقُ». The fourth: that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of «يُفْرَق», i.e. "distinguishing". The fifth: that it is a maṣdar of an omitted «أَمَرْنا». The sixth: that «يُفْرَقُ» has the sense of «يَأْمُر». The difference between this and what preceded: here you return the governing agent to the maṣdar, and in what preceded, the reverse. The seventh: that it is a ḥāl from «كُلُّ». The eighth: that it is a ḥāl from «أَمْرٍ», and that is permitted because it is described. Except that in it are two things: the coming of the ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi in cases other than those mentioned; and second, that it is confirmatory. The ninth: that it is a maṣdar of «أَنْزَل», i.e. "We sent it down a sending down". Al-Akhfash said this. The tenth: that it is a maṣdar, but with the governing agent interpreted in its meaning, i.e. "We commanded it a command by reason of the sending down", as they said that in the two analyses «فيها يُفْرَقُ فَرْقاً» or «يَنْزِل إنزالاً». The eleventh: that it is accusative as specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and he does not mean by it the technical ikhtiṣāṣ, since that is not indefinite. The twelfth: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «حكيم». The thirteenth: that it is accusative as a direct object of «مُنْذِرين», like His saying {لِّيُنْذِرَ بَأْساً شَدِيداً} [al-Kahf: 2], with the first object omitted, i.e. "warning the people of a command". [Translator's note: the source says "twelve" but lists thirteen.] The sum is that its accusative returns to four things: the direct object, the object of purpose, the maṣdar, and the ḥāl; the multiplicity is only according to the positions, and you have known them from what I have set before you.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أَمْرٌ» nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It strengthens the accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ."

His saying: «مِنْ عِنْدِنا»: it may be attached to «يُفْرَقُ», i.e. "from Our side", and it is for the beginning of the range figuratively. It may also be an adjective of «أَمْراً».

His saying: {إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ}: a third answer, or resumptive, or a badal from His saying {إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ}.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {رَحْمَةً}: it has five analyses. [The first:] a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. Its governing agent is either «أَنْزَلْناه», or «أَمْراً», or «يُفْرَقُ», or «مُنْذِرين». The second: a maṣdar of an implied verb, i.e. "We showed mercy, a mercy". The third: an object of «مُرْسِلين». The fourth: a ḥāl from the pronoun of «مُرْسِلين», i.e. "possessors of mercy". The fifth: that it is a badal from «أَمْراً», so what preceded applies to it, and the analyses of it become many.

«مِنْ رَبِّك» is attached to «رَحْمة», or to an omitted element as an adjective. In «مِنْ ربِّك» there is a shift (iltifāt) from the first person to the third; had it followed the pattern of what preceded, He would have said: "a mercy from Us".

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {رَبِّ السماوات}: the Kufans read «رَبّ» genitive, and the others nominative. The genitive is as a badal, or explication (bayān), or adjective. The nominative is on an implied mubtadaʾ, or on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَآئِكُمُ}: the majority read it nominative as a badal, explication or adjective of «ربُّ السماوات» for those who read it nominative, or on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, or a khabar after a khabar of His saying {إِنَّهُ هُوَ السميع}, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ according to all, I mean the readers of the genitive and the nominative, or the agent of His saying «يُميت». In «يُحْيي» there is a pronoun that refers back to what precedes, i.e. "He gives life", that is, the Lord of the heavens, "and He causes death", so the overt noun is put where the pronoun belongs. It may be that «يُحيي ويُميت» is an instance of conflict (tanāzuʿ). The nominative may be attributed to the first or the second, like «يَقُوم ويَقْعد زيد», and this is what Abū l-Baqāʾ meant by his saying: "or on the condition of explanation".

Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Ḥasan read it genitive / as a badal, explication or adjective of «رب السماوات», and this requires them to read «رَبِّ السماوات» genitive. Al-Anṭākī read it accusative as praise.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ تَأْتِي}: accusative by «ارْتَقِبْ» as an adverbial. The object is omitted, i.e. "await the promise of Allah on that day". It may also be that it is itself the object awaited.
